corrections.claimed_speedup: Geometric-mean speedup of 5.91x on CPU (16 cores) and 7.4x on Xeon Phi (32 cores) relative to KLU; up to 53x on CPU (16 cores) and 13.3x on Xeon Phi (32 cores) over Intel MKL PARDISO for low fill-in circuit matrices (paper abstract as quoted in search results; paper not opened).
corrections.caveats: Numbers come from the abstract of the Basker paper (arXiv 1601.05725; journal version Parallel Computing 2017, doi 10.1016/j.parco.2017.06.003) as quoted in WebSearch results; the paper itself could not be opened (arxiv, sciencedirect, osti.gov, adsabs are egress-blocked), so flags, CPU models and the matrix set are unseen. The 5.91x/7.4x KLU figures are geometric means; the 53x/13.3x PARDISO figures are maxima on low-fill circuit matrices, where supernodal PARDISO is a weak fit. Basker's README.txt in the repo lists tested systems (Intel Sandy, Intel Phi, IBM Power8) and has no benchmark numbers or harness ('Compiler Option Flags: NA'). License: the Basker sources and packages/shylu/LICENSE carry 'SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause'. Numbers date from 2016 hardware and the 2016-17 code; the canonical URL is the Trilinos monorepo (Basker lives in packages/shylu/shylu_node/basker).

notes: benchmark_url set to the arXiv preprint whose abstract carries the numbers (search results; not opened, arxiv is blocked); journal version is Parallel Computing 2017 (doi 10.1016/j.parco.2017.06.003). No benchmark_url exists in the repo; the numbers rest on the abstract only.
